sealed.statement: Graceful node shutdown after a managed partition split terminates the process cleanly with no live timers or open handles, demonstrated by the call-binding-account-summary example runner exiting without its bounded-exit workaround and by a focused shutdown regression test.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

claim: Reproduced the sealed symptom on current HEAD (seal-freshness advisory discharged) and disproved the sealed root-cause attribution. Empirical matrix on the call-binding-account-summary runner: (A) full example (split+deploy) hangs after shutdown with exactly 3 live MessagePort handles, no timers; (B) split WITHOUT deploy exits cleanly with zero handles; (C) deploy WITHOUT split hangs with the same 3 MessagePorts. Handles are request/call-cell Worker ports (src/runtime/wasi-component-cell-runtime.js:221): no node-teardown path reaches ServiceRuntimeLifecycle/driver stop, so cell workers are never terminated (runtime-service-handler.shutdown only clears maps; bootstrap seed-cleanup stops owners but never stops replicas). The 'background retry/cleanup timers' comment in the runner dates to the example's authoring commit c06ee7de7 and was already stale: all split-merge-manager timers are unref'd (evaluation-methods.js:51,108; transition-methods.js ~325), and split timers do NOT leak (probe B). The real defect is missing cell-worker teardown at node shutdown, which is split-independent. This quest as sealed (fix split timers, remove the workaround) would fix the wrong mechanism; the lever is a ServiceRuntimeLifecycle/WasmComponentDriver stop-all wired into node shutdown — outside this quest's sealed scope. Altitude reflection: EXHAUST this quest and author the higher-altitude quest for cell-worker teardown ownership (which then legitimately removes the runner workaround).

attempt.hypothesis: Measured attempt on the sealed frontier: built the 3-variant empirical matrix over the call-binding-account-summary runner ((A) split+deploy: hang with 3 MessagePorts, zero timers; (B) split-only: clean exit, zero handles; (C) deploy-only: hang with the same 3 MessagePorts) proving the sealed split-timer root cause false and locating the leak in request/call-cell worker teardown (no shutdown path reaches WasiComponentCellRuntime._stop/worker.terminate). No source change: the sealed mechanism does not exist; the finding log carries the full evidence.

note: Altitude reflection on the sealed frame. The quest frame says: managed split leaves live timers/handles; fix split shutdown ownership; then the account-summary runner exits without its bounded-exit workaround. Measured evidence (finding 2026-08-05T20:18:26Z) refutes the frame's causal attribution: the hang is caused by request/call-cell Worker MessagePorts never terminated at node shutdown, and is fully reproducible with NO split (deploy-only variant hangs identically), while a split WITHOUT service deploy exits cleanly with zero residual handles. The sealed symptom (runner does not exit naturally) is real, but the sealed mechanism (split timers/handles) is absent on HEAD — every split-merge timer is unref'd and none survive in the matrix. Fixing anything inside this quest's split-shutdown scope cannot move the probe: the runner would still hang on the cell workers. The honest move is PARK/EXHAUST-AND-PIVOT: park this quest's frontier (kind exhausted, provenance operator), and author the higher-altitude quest 'cell-worker teardown ownership at node shutdown' (ServiceRuntimeLifecycle/driver stop-all wired into bootstrap teardown; owner boundary identified in the finding: WasiComponentCellRuntime.cells has no stop-all; RuntimeServiceHandler.shutdown clears maps without stopping replicas), whose doneWhen is exactly the workaround-free natural exit this quest's statement wanted. That successor quest legitimately removes the runner workaround as its proof.

No honest move exists inside the sealed split-shutdown scope: every split-merge timer is unref'd, none survive shutdown, and fixing split-side shutdown cannot make the runner exit while cell workers leak. Pivot: author the higher-altitude cell-worker-teardown quest (owner boundary: WasiComponentCellRuntime.cells / ServiceRuntimeLifecycle stop-all wired into bootstrap seed/join cleanup), which inherits this quest's terminal proof goal — the account-summary runner exiting naturally without the SHUTDOWN_BOUND_MS race and explicit process.exit.
